title_en: The Story of Mid-Autumn Festival - August 15th

full_text_zh:
[P1] 中秋节的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 中秋节的故事
司南/改编
刘大为/绘画

中秋节晚上，合家围
坐在一起，吃着瓜果，听
奶奶讲那过去的事情。

连环画出版社

[P3] 很久很久以前，天上有十个太阳。它们把土地晒得冒烟，把庄稼烤得枯焦，老百姓热得活不下去了。

有个人名字叫羿。他的力气特别大，能够拉开万斤宝弓，射死大蛇和猛兽。

[P4] 羿看到百姓太可怜了，
就用足力气弯弓搭箭，一口气射下了九个太阳。最后一个太阳吓得认了错，羿才留下它，让它早出晚归，为百姓多做好事。

从那以后羿成了人人敬仰的英雄，他的名字传遍天下。

[P5] 羿娶了嫦娥姑娘为妻，他们相亲相爱，过着幸福的生活。

嫦娥美丽、勤劳，心地善良。她常把羿猎到的野兽分给乡亲们。

[P6] 有一天，羿上山打猎，遇到一位道士。道士对羿说：“你为百姓除害，立下了功劳。我送你一包神药，要是吃上半包，就会长生不老；要是全都吃下去，就会成仙升天。”
羿把神药拿回家，告诉嫦娥：“你好好保管这包药。我们找个良辰吉日，一起吃了它。这样，我们夫妻就能长生不老，永不分离。”

[P7] 羿是射下九个太阳的大英雄，很多人来找他学习武艺。他的徒弟里有一个叫逢蒙的人，这是个坏家伙。

逢蒙知道羿的家里藏着神药，他暗暗打着坏主意。

[P8] 这一年八月十五，
羿带徒弟们出去打猎。

傍晚，逢蒙一个人偷偷溜回来，闯进羿的家里，
逼着嫦娥交出神药。嫦娥大声呼救，可是羿打猎还没回来，周围也没有别的人家。

[P9] 嫦娥急了，心想：‘绝不能让无耻的逢蒙抢到神药。’她打开药包，把药全部吞进嘴里。
突然，嫦娥的身体变得像羽毛一样轻。她不由自主地飞出窗口，向天空飞去。

[P10] 天空无边无际，可怜的嫦娥啊，不知飞向何方，在月亮上也许能看到自己的亲人吧？慢慢地，嫦娥飞向月亮，从此住在广寒宫里。
羿回家后听说这件事，赶紧追出门去，可已经太晚了！只见圆圆的月亮上，隐约有嫦娥的影子。乡亲们安慰他说：“嫦娥还会回来的，等等吧。”

[P11] 第二年八月十五，羿拿出嫦娥爱吃的水果，还做了圆圆的月饼，盼望嫦娥回家。

一年又一年过去了，嫦娥始终没有回来。慢慢地，大家都按照后羿的习惯，每到八月十五，就准备月饼、水果，祭拜月亮。

[P12] 农历八月是秋天中间的一个月，十五日又是这个月中间的头一天，所以八月十五就叫中秋节。每到中秋节，一家人都要团聚，所以，中秋节也叫团圆节。

中秋节成为民间节日，是从唐代开始的。嫦娥的故事只是中秋传说的一个版本，还有人说唐明皇曾在八月十五的夜晚，梦游月宫，得到仙女传授的仙乐，并把它带回人间。这个故事也十分优美动人。

到了宋代，中秋节已经十分兴盛，也开始重视家人团圆。苏轼的《水调歌头》千古传诵：
“明月几时有，把酒问青天。不知天上宫阙，今夕是何年……人有悲欢离合，月有阴晴圆缺，此事古难全。但愿人长久，千里共婵娟。”

明、清时期，老百姓中已经流行中秋拜月的仪式。北方拜月多贴“月光马儿”，就是用秫秸杆儿架起的神像纸，还供奉月饼和切成莲花状的西瓜等，并向月亮诵读祭文。老北京有一种特殊的工艺品“兔儿爷”，也在中秋这一天上市。人形兔脸，武将打扮，身披金盔金甲，大红战袍，有的背上还插着伞盖，有的手拿大刀，有的骑着

[P13] 各种各样的动物，有的嘴上或胳膊上还有提线，可以动弹。除了兔儿爷，还有兔儿奶奶。它们都是泥制彩绘的，非常精细，既是神像，又是孩子们喜爱的玩具。

广西毛南族还有“射月亮”的活动：月亮升起时，在凉台上摆一张八仙桌，桌边捆一根削尖了头的竹竿，上面插一个柚子，柚子上还插着三炷香。让柚子和香都对着月亮，就是“射月亮”。人们在桌前做出种种仪式，请月神降临，还要对歌问答，直到天快亮时才散去。

许多少数民族在中秋节这天庆丰收，祭祀农耕之神，吃新米，其中不少民族还要特别厚待狗。因为传说人类得罪了天神、失去谷种之后，是狗把谷种要了回来，才让人们不至于饿死。

中秋是收获的季节。除了尝新粮、吃晚熟瓜果这些应时活动外，唐宋时有桂圆、莲子和藕粉等制成的“玩月羹”，南方人常在中秋吃桂花，吃莼菜、鲈鱼，吃芋头、柚子，吃螃蟹、鸭子等等。金风阵阵的晚上，吃着这些美味，看着头顶圆圆的月亮，不由得要感叹：“多么美好的生活啊！”，

full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of the Mid-Autumn Festival
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of the Mid-Autumn Festival
Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Liu Dawei

On Mid-Autumn Festival evening, the whole family gathers together, eating melons and fruits, listening to Grandma tell stories from the past.

Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P3] Long, long ago, there were ten suns in the sky. They scorched the land until it smoked, baked the crops until they withered, and the common people were too hot to survive.

There was a man named Yi. He was incredibly strong, able to draw a bow of ten thousand jin, and shoot down giant snakes and fierce beasts.

[P4] Yi saw how pitiful the people were,
so he used all his strength to draw his bow and arrow, and in one breath shot down nine suns. The last sun, frightened, admitted its mistake, so Yi spared it, letting it rise early and set late, to do good deeds for the people.

From then on, Yi became a hero admired by everyone, and his name spread throughout the world.

[P5] Yi married the girl Chang'e as his wife. They loved each other deeply and lived a happy life.

Chang'e was beautiful, hardworking, and kind-hearted. She often shared the wild animals Yi hunted with the villagers.

[P6] One day, Yi went hunting in the mountains and met a Taoist. The Taoist said to Yi, "You have rid the people of harm and achieved great merit. I will give you a packet of magic medicine. If you eat half of it, you will live forever; if you eat it all, you will become an immortal and ascend to heaven." 
Yi took the magic medicine home and told Chang'e, "Take good care of this medicine. Let's find a favorable day and eat it together. This way, we, husband and wife, can live forever and never be separated."

[P7] Yi was the great hero who shot down nine suns. Many people came to him to learn martial arts. Among his disciples was a man named Fengmeng, a bad fellow.

Fengmeng knew that Yi's home hid the elixir of immortality. He secretly harbored evil intentions.

[P8] On the fifteenth day of the eighth month this year,
Yi took his apprentices out hunting.

In the evening, Fengmeng sneaked back alone, broke into Yi's home,
forced Chang'e to hand over the elixir. Chang'e cried out for help, but Yi hadn't returned from hunting yet, and there were no other houses nearby.

[P9] Chang'e panicked, thinking: 'I must not let the shameless Fengmeng get his hands on the magic medicine.' She opened the medicine pouch and swallowed all the pills.
Suddenly, Chang'e's body became as light as feathers. She involuntarily flew out of the window and soared toward the sky.

[P10] The sky is boundless. Poor Chang'e, not knowing where she is flying, perhaps on the moon she can see her loved ones? Slowly, Chang'e flies toward the moon and from then on lives in the Cold Palace.
After Yi returned home and heard what had happened, he rushed out to chase after her, but it was already too late! He saw only a faint shadow of Chang'e on the round moon. The villagers comforted him: "Chang'e will come back, just wait a little longer."

[P11] On the fifteenth day of the eighth month the following year, Yi took out the fruits Chang'e loved to eat and made round mooncakes, hoping Chang'e would come home.

Year after year passed, but Chang'e never returned. Gradually, everyone followed Yi's custom, preparing mooncakes and fruits every August 15th to worship the moon.

[P12] The eighth month of the lunar calendar is the middle month of autumn, and the 15th day is the middle day of that month, so the 15th of the eighth month is called the Mid-Autumn Festival. Every Mid-Autumn Festival, families gather together, so the festival is also called the Reunion Festival.

The Mid-Autumn Festival became a folk festival starting in the Tang Dynasty. The story of Chang'e is just one version of the Mid-Autumn legend. Some also say that Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang Dynasty once dreamed of visiting the Moon Palace on the night of the 15th of the eighth month, received celestial music from a fairy, and brought it back to the human world. This story is also very beautiful and touching.

By the Song Dynasty, the Mid-Autumn Festival had become very popular, and people began to emphasize family reunions. Su Shi's "Water Melody: Ode to the Moon" has been passed down through the ages: 
"When will the bright moon appear? I raise my wine cup and ask the sky. I don't know what year it is in the celestial palace tonight... People experience joys and sorrows, partings and reunions; the moon has its bright and dark, its full and waning phases—this has always been hard to perfect. May we all live long, and share the beauty of the moon even if we are thousands of miles apart."

During the Ming and Qing dynasties, the custom of worshipping the moon during Mid-Autumn became popular among the common people. In northern China, people often pasted "Moonlight Horses"—paper effigies mounted on bamboo sticks—and offered mooncakes and watermelons cut into lotus shapes, while reciting prayers to the moon. In old Beijing, there was a special craft called "Tuer爷" (Rabbit God), which was also sold on Mid-Autumn Day. These figures had rabbit faces and were dressed as warriors, wearing golden helmets and armor, and red battle robes. Some had parasols on their backs, some held big swords, and some were riding

[P13] Various kinds of animals, some with strings on their mouths or arms, can move. Besides the Moon Rabbit, there's also the Moon Rabbit's grandmother. They are all made of clay and painted, very detailed, serving as both religious figures and toys beloved by children.

The Maonan people of Guangxi have a 'shooting the moon' activity: when the moon rises, they set up an eight-legged table on a veranda, tie a sharpened bamboo pole to the side, place a pomelo on top, and insert three incense sticks into the pomelo. Pointing the pomelo and incense toward the moon is called 'shooting the moon'. People perform various rituals before the table, invite the moon god to descend, and sing songs and answer questions until nearly dawn before dispersing.

Many ethnic minorities celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival by harvesting, worshipping the god of agriculture, and eating new rice. Some even treat dogs especially well, because legend says that after humans offended the heavenly gods and lost their grain seeds, it was the dog who retrieved the seeds, preventing people from starving.

Mid-Autumn is the season of harvest. Besides tasting new grain and eating late-ripening fruits, during the Tang and Song dynasties, there was a 'moon-viewing porridge' made from longan, lotus seeds, and lotus root starch. In the south, people often eat osmanthus flowers, water shield, mandarin fish, taro, pomelo, crabs, ducks, and more during the Mid-Autumn Festival. On evenings with a gentle autumn breeze, eating these delicacies and gazing at the round moon above, one can't help but exclaim: 'What a wonderful life!'

full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《中秋节的故事》的封面，画面中一位身着绿衣的女子在云间飘浮，背景为明亮的黄色天空，下方标有书名和出版社名称。
[P2] 本页为绘本《中秋节的故事》的扉页，左侧显示书名、作者和出版社信息，右侧画面描绘中秋节夜晚，一家人在葡萄藤下围坐，吃着瓜果，听奶奶讲述过去的故事。
[P3] 本页讲述了远古时代天上有十个太阳，导致大地干涸、百姓苦不堪言，随后引出一位名叫羿的英雄，他力大无穷，能拉开万斤宝弓，射杀猛兽。
[P4] 羿射下九个太阳，留下一个为百姓造福，从此成为人人敬仰的英雄。
[P5] 本页讲述了羿与嫦娥结婚后过上幸福生活，嫦娥美丽勤劳，常将羿猎得的野兽分给乡亲们。
[P6] 羿在打猎时遇到一位道士，获赠一包神药，道士说明药效；羿回家后将神药交给嫦娥，并计划择日共同服用以求长生不老、永不分离。
[P7] 本页介绍了羿的徒弟逢蒙是个坏人，并揭示他得知羿家中藏有神药后，心生歹念。
[P8] 本页讲述羿在八月十五带徒弟外出打猎，而逢蒙趁机潜入羿家，逼迫嫦娥交出神药，嫦娥呼救却无人能助。
[P9] 嫦娥为保护神药不被逢蒙抢走，情急之下将药全部吞下，随即身体变轻，飞向天空。
[P10] 嫦娥吞下神药后飞向月亮，最终定居广寒宫；羿赶回家中发现为时已晚，只能望着月亮上的影子，乡亲们安慰他等待嫦娥归来。
[P11] 羿在八月十五准备水果和月饼，盼望嫦娥归来；随着时间推移，人们沿袭此习俗，每年八月十五祭拜月亮，纪念嫦娥。
[P12] 本页介绍了中秋节的由来、历史演变及民间习俗，解释了为何称其为团圆节，并提及唐明皇梦游月宫、苏轼《水调歌头》、北方拜月仪式及“兔儿爷”等文化元素。
[P13] 本页介绍了中秋节的民俗活动，如广西毛南族的“射月亮”、少数民族祭祀农耕之神、南方人食用的中秋美食等，并列举了“毛毛虫童书馆”系列丛书的书目，最后附有图书的CIP数据。
